comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
The best practice for reproducible random simulations is to create a seeded RNG (not touching the global one) and passing it around.  (See e.g. https://blog.scientific-python.org/numpy/numpy-rng/)

We aspire for all code to offer a default `rng` keyword which defaults to `np.random`, see e.g. `ase.md.velocitydistribution`.

Unfortunately I can see that the minimahopping module does not offer an rng keyword, forcing the caller to seed the global generator.  Since that's unintended would you mind adding an `rng` keyword to minimahopping so the user can control randomness without touching the global generator?  Something like:

```
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
MinimaHopping(..., rng=rng)
```

comments.author: HannaTuerk
comments.body: Thanks for the suggestions and careful reading of the example @askhl , adding a rng to the function is a good idea, I will add it to the function and test it! :)
